== Adding P5137 to lexemes by using Wiktionary translation clusters ==

I'm running an experiment where I use basic translation data from Wiktionary (via my [https://www.wikdict.com WikDict] project) to add P5137 to lexemes that don't have any such link yet and have exactly one sense.

Basic concept:

# Find translation on Wiktionary where one end of the translation already has a P5137. Then the same relation is a candidate for the other end of the translation. Problem: words can be ambiguous.
# Get the description of the lexeme's sense and the labels and descriptions of the assigned item (all CC0 from Wikidata). Let an LLM verify this assignment to rule out most bad matches.
# Let a human go through the remaining items and assign approve/reject/defer labels. Only approved ones are queued for writing. The results are also stored for evaluation and future improvements.
# Write to Wikidata

'''Licensing''': Wiktionary (CC-BY-SA) contributes only facts — which lemmas cluster, and the lemmas themselves. Verification reads only the anchor item's CC0 label/description, never the Wiktionary gloss, and nothing from Wiktionary (gloss, translation, sense numbering) is ever written to Wikidata. To my understanding, this clears all licensing hurdles.

'''Examples''':

* Dorsch (de) → [[Q13194939]] (cod) — [[Special:Diff/2511864531]]
* Englischlehrer (de) → [[Q101444631]] (English teacher) — [[Special:Diff/2511864533]]
* Bosnier (de) → [[Q99907279]] (Bosnians and Herzegovinians) — [[Special:Diff/2511864525]]
* Existenz (de) → [[Q468777]] (existence) — [[Special:Diff/2511864539]]

'''Questions''':

# Do you agree that the licensing is ok?

# If this is generally ok, what is the best way to proceed? Should I slowly (<100 items/week, even less at first) push more manually approved items as assisted writes?
